ideas.title: The Hidden Code Exposing Your Phone's Real Owner
ideas.angle: The video shows the viewer how to enter a specific USSD code to reveal hidden diagnostic menus that show how many times their battery has been cycled and if their data is being synced to an external server. It triggers comments by asking users to post their battery cycle count.

hook.en: Type this code to see who's tracking you.

ideas.reason: Utility-based tech secrets (USSD codes) consistently hit 80%+ VVSA because they offer an immediate, interactive task. With rising concerns over digital privacy and planned obsolescence, 'battery health' and 'tracking' are high-velocity triggers.
sources: ZDNet: Hidden iPhone and Android codes
Apple Support: Battery Cycle Count monitoring
FCC: Guide on USSD codes and privacy

ideas.title: The 1-Second Pupil Glitch That Exposes Liars
ideas.angle: Explains the 'Cognitive Load' reflex where pupils dilate when the brain is processing a lie or complex AI-generated response. It challenges the viewer to look at their own eyes in a mirror while telling a lie, forcing a rewatch and high engagement.

hook.en: Your pupils grow when you lie.

ideas.reason: Social power and micro-behavior decoding are evergreen. This specific 'glitch' is visceral and easy to test immediately, driving high Average Percentage Viewed (APV) as viewers try to observe the effect.
sources: Psychological Science: Pupil dilation as an index of cognitive load
CIA Manual of Trickery and Deception: Physiological markers of stress
Nature: AI versus human eye-tracking patterns

ideas.title: The Scary Setting Uploading Your Screen Right Now
ideas.angle: Reveals the 'Screen Recording' or 'App Privacy Report' features on modern smartphones that show which apps are silently taking screenshots or accessing the clipboard. It commands the viewer to turn off 'Share iPhone/Android Analytics' immediately.

hook.en: Turn off this one setting immediately.

ideas.reason: The 'Illegal to know' archetype combined with an urgent command ('Turn off...') creates a massive pattern interrupt. Privacy-focused tech shorts are currently exploding due to recent OS updates highlighting data transparency.
sources: Wired: How to check which apps are spying on your screen
Android Developers: Privacy Sandbox and screen recording permissions
